subject: DPA & SCCs: redlines, delegation matrix, and sign-off plan (ACME Cloud)
messages:
From: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@acmecloud.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai; ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: DPA and SCCs - initial redline request

Hi Jonas / Ben,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Attached is ACME's standard DPA redline and our SCCs confirmation sheet (see attached in separate email from legal).

Two asks to start:
- Can Redwood review ACME's redline and confirm which changes are acceptable vs. material (we're particularly watching liability, international transfer language, and KMS access).
- We need a short execution plan for SCCs: will Redwood adopt the European Commission standard SCCs, or do we need a transfer-impact addendum approach? Acme's procurement needs this answered before they issue a PO.

Our timelines: legal sign-off by end of next week (2026-11-20) to hit a Nov billing start.

Attaching ACME redline as a placeholder (we'll forward the formal doc from Gabe).

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m sync if that helps.

Elena Moreno
Director, Strategic Contracts
ACME Cloud

[Attachment stub: ACME_DPA_redline_20261114.docx (docx)]

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-14T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA and SCCs - initial redline request

Elena —

Appreciate the heads up. We'll take a first-pass redline and a practical execution plan for SCCs. High level: Redwood can sign the EU Commission SCCs (2024 clause set) and map our subprocessor/hosting regions, but a couple of ACME redlines will require coordination with Product (KMS scope, export controls) or an exec exception (liability cap carveout). I'll outline accepts vs. discussion points and propose a mutual action plan.

Next steps from our side:
1) Ben will run the legal redline and produce a tracked-response.
2) I'll attach a delegation matrix showing recommended controller/processor roles for ACME's use-case and a checklist for evidence (SOC2 artifacts, KMS attestation, export path).
3) Laura will confirm procurement/DocuSign and whether finance needs a PO before countersign.

Can you confirm whether ACME requires Private/VPC hosting (that affects SCCs and KMS scope) or if hosted (multi-tenant) is acceptable?

I'll attach our response shortly.

- Jonas Weber
Head of Legal Partnerships | Redwood Inference

[Attachment stub: Redwood_DPA_response_20261114.docx (docx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@acmecloud.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA and SCCs - redline + delegation matrix (ACME)

On Mon, Nov 14, 2026 at 11:03 AM jonas.weber@redwood.ai wrote:
> Jonas —
> Appreciate the heads up. We'll take a first-pass redline...

Elena / team — attached are two things from Legal/Privacy:
- delegation_matrix_ACME_20261115.csv (proposed controller/processor split and recommended subprocessor gating)
- SCCs_execution_plan_20261115.pdf (practical steps to adopt SCCs + mapping to our infra regions)

Quick summary of redline positions (from Redwood_DPA_response_20261114.docx):
- Accept: definitions alignment, data subject rights cooperation language, routine security controls sections.
- Discuss: 
  * Liability cap language (ACME asks for unlimited liability on security incidents tied to data residency) — propose carveout tied to willful misconduct or gross negligence only.
  * KMS access: we can provide customer-managed keys on Dedicated/Private but not for hosted multi-tenant without an add-on.
  * Transfer impact: we'll adopt SCCs; if ACME requires a transfer-impact addendum with additional controls we can include an appendix describing our encryption and export controls.

Propose a 30m legal + product call tomorrow (2026-11-16 10:00 PT) to resolve KMS scope and liability cap. If ACME confirms VPC requirement, that materially changes the execution path and timeline.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy | Redwood Inference

[Attachments: delegation_matrix_ACME_20261115.csv, SCCs_execution_plan_20261115.pdf]

From: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@acmecloud.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com; Gabe Lin <gabe.lin@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T15:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA and SCCs - redline + delegation matrix (ACME)

Ben / Jonas —

Thanks for the detailed notes and the delegation matrix. A few quick updates from Acme:
- Procurement can issue the PO on 2026-11-18 provided legal clears language by EOD 2026-11-17.
- ACME would prefer Redwood to adopt the SCCs rather than a bespoke transfer-addendum; that said, they want the KMS commitment documented in the order form if Dedicated/VPC is required.
- On liability: ACME's legal asks for a higher cap for security incidents related to regulated data. Can Redwood provide a timeboxed limited exception? If so, procurement can pull a 10% volume credit in exchange for a short SLA exception. Gabe will share the formal redline shortly.

We'll schedule the 30m call for 2026-11-16 10:00 PT — Gabe and I will join.

Attaching PO draft for internal reference. Please send the DocuSign link when ready.

Elena

[Attachment stub: Acme_PO_20261115.pdf (pdf)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Moreno <elena.moreno@acmecloud.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai; ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA and SCCs - redline + delegation matrix (ACME)

Elena —

Thanks — quick update from Redwood ops/finance: exec team approves a one-time limited SLA exception tied to the order (internal memo attached to deal). We can accept an increased liability cap for security incidents limited to the contracted project and timeboxed to 12 months post-ship, provided ACME signs the dedicated order form and confirms VPC/Dedicated deployment (so we can enable customer-managed KMS).

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/rdw-acme-20261116
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/458-RDW (deal RDW-2026-ACME-458)
Evidence folder (SOC2 + KMS attestation) has been shared: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-evidence

Next asks for ACME:
- Confirm hosting choice (Hosted vs Dedicated/VPC) by EOD 2026-11-17.
- Confirm acceptance of delegation_matrix_ACME_20261115.csv or propose edits in the next 24 hours.

Once we have those, I'll route the redline to Exec for final countersign and send the DocuSign packet.

Laura Bennett
Director, Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
[Attachment stub: RDW_exec_memo_sla_exception_20261116.pdf (pdf)]
